newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan spring crop growth ahead of 92/96 avg.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan spring crop growth ahead of 92/96 avg.

text.p: Saskatchewan spring crop growth is ahead of the five-year 1992/96 average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly crop report.

Twenty five percent of spring cereals were at or past the shotblade stage compared to the average 14 percent. Fifty seven percent of flax past the seedling stage compared with the average of 37 percent. Seventy five percent of canola was at or past the seedling stage compared to the average of 51 percent. Thirty eight percent of fall cereals were in the dough stage versus the average of 25 percent.
Crop damage was mainly weather related.
Drought damage was reported in many south and some central areas. North and central regions that saw heavy rain reported some flooding along with localized hail damage.
Insect damage was minimal in the past week.

An average 5 mm (0.2 inch) of rain fell on the southern grainbelt with up to 25 mm (1 inch) around Redvers. Drought damage was reported across the south grainbelt and most pronounced in the south-central and southeast.
Central Saskatchewan reported an average of 11 mm (0.4 inch) of rain, but Quill Lake and Young saw 40 mm (1.6 inch). Drought was hard on crops in the east central area.
Northern districts saw an average 20 mm (0.8 inch) of rain as Makwa saw 35 mm (1.4 inch). Heavy rains caused some flood damage throughout the region.
